title: Software Engineering Is Becoming Factory Engineering — Zach Lloyd, Warp
talk_summary: Zach Lloyd argues software engineering is shifting from interactive agents to automated 'software factories' — a graph of triage, spec, implement, review, verify, monitor steps with humans inserted at defined checkpoints. The concrete mechanisms are observer agents that improve skills from human corrections, spec-driven development (product spec + tech spec), and measuring factory efficiency in human time and token time.

takeaways.technique: Observer agents that rewrite skills from human corrections
takeaways.what_they_do: Factory agents run skills; separate observer agents watch where those skills fail or where a senior engineer corrects an agent's output, then update the skill for the next run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you'd want an observer agent that would look at that and basically uh improve the code review agent for the next run

takeaways.technique: Agent-first review, human review as risk management
takeaways.what_they_do: Run an agent code review before any human, then treat human review as a risk-management decision about which changes warrant it rather than a default gate on everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I would have an agent do code review first and then it becomes over time like a riskmanagement exercise of like when do you bring in humans to do code review

takeaways.technique: Triage agent that auto-implements unambiguous issues
takeaways.what_they_do: A triage agent inspects incoming issues and, if easy and unambiguous, implements directly; only hard issues get routed to spec-writing agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if this is easy and this is unambiguous, just implement it and this is how you can actually get going with a factory

takeaways.technique: Split product spec and tech spec
takeaways.what_they_do: For hard issues, one agent writes a product spec (invariants the product must satisfy) and a separate tech spec (architecture and shape of the code) before implementation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: having an agent write what we call a product spec and a tech spec. Product spec describes the product invariance

takeaways.technique: Measure factory efficiency in human time and token time
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat the factory as a process to be measured: track software shipped against cost in human time and token time, then improve the ratio over time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how much software did you ship? How much did it cost in terms of human time and token time and you're going to want to measure this

takeaways.technique: Explicit human checkpoints in the loop graph
takeaways.what_they_do: Model the SDLC as a graph with named steps and mark exactly where humans step in (spec review, code review, product review) rather than leaving intervention ad hoc.
takeaways.evidence_quote: these little blue boxes are where humans step in. Humans will review the spec
